cands.name: Carolyn G. Logan
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina House District 101 (Mecklenburg County) since January 2019. Before that she was an Asheville police officer from 1977 and a North Carolina Highway Patrol trooper from 1984 until she retired in 2007. She was the state's first Black female trooper.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended in the 2026 cycle by the voter guides Beyond The Ballot (Sway voting group by Niayai Lavien) and NC Public School Champions (Sway voting group by Taylor/PublicEdTay).

cands.gaps: Her birthplace and the year she came to North Carolina were not found. The pages gathered gave no documented stance or action from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, guns, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site speaks only in general terms of public safety, health insurance, broadband and free school lunch. Her sponsored-bills table on Ballotpedia came through empty, and the campaign site's 'Record in the Legislature', 'Bills Introduced' and 'Endorsements' pages were not available. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any cycle from 2020 to 2026. No data-center or development statements were found. No controversies or foreign ties were found in these pages.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign biography says she grew up in Asheville, NC, and she then worked in North Carolina law enforcement for about 30 years; her birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elected to the NC House in 2018 and re-elected through 2026, so she has served about seven years. Before that she spent roughly 30 years in law enforcement: Asheville police from 1977 and the NC Highway Patrol from 1984 to 2007, rising to sergeant and later serving as a Traffic Safety Specialist. She is a certified Basic Law Enforcement Instructor.
qual.why: Several terms of prior legislative service put her in the high range. Her career was in law enforcement and traffic safety rather than law, policy or budget work, and committee seats were not counted.
